topic: What is the RBI repo rate and how does it affect borrowers?
guide_persona: Riya — a friendly, knowledgeable 28-year-old who works in finance and loves explaining money concepts to beginners.
learner_persona: Arjun — a curious 16-year-old who has just started paying attention to money and asks honest, relatable questions.

dialogue.speaker: LEARNER
dialogue.text: Riya didi, I saw in the news that RBI changed the repo rate to 5.50%. What even is a repo rate, and does it affect my parents' home loan EMI?

dialogue.speaker: GUIDE
dialogue.text: Great question, Arjun! Your parents took a home loan at a floating rate. That means whenever RBI changes a key rate called the 'repo rate', their monthly EMI can go up or down — sometimes without any notice.

dialogue.speaker: GUIDE
dialogue.text: The repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends money to banks. When RBI sets it at 5.50%, it becomes cheaper or costlier for banks to borrow. Banks then adjust your home loan interest rate accordingly — that's what makes it 'floating'.

dialogue.speaker: GUIDE
dialogue.text: Say the repo rate is 5.50% today. If RBI increases it next quarter, your bank may raise your home loan rate. As per RBI rules, your bank must inform you at sanction about these possible changes — and send you a quarterly statement showing your remaining EMIs.

dialogue.speaker: GUIDE
dialogue.text: If you don't know about this, a sudden EMI increase feels like a shock. But here's the good news: RBI now mandates that your bank must clearly communicate any rate-change impact at the time they give you the loan — so you can plan ahead.

dialogue.speaker: GUIDE
dialogue.text: If your family has a floating-rate home loan, ask your bank for the quarterly statement that shows the current rate, EMIs paid, and EMIs remaining. This is your right under RBI rules — and it helps you plan your budget better.
